A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spacetime information-geometry framework and retain matching methods and experiments despite the changed title and organization. All 23 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v2, including figures, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture trajectory experiments, ImageNet image interpolations, and alanine-dipeptide transition-path experiments, including constrained paths and additional appendix visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains original trajectory and transition-path experiments and adds image-similarity correlations, molecular baseline results, and qualitative comparisons in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The denoiser-moment/JVP energy estimator, geodesic optimization, annealed Langevin sampler, and variance/region penalties are retained. v1 Equation 23 and v2 Equation 14 express the same estimator. DiffED applies the already-defined geodesic length to image similarity; its name and evaluation do not establish a changed underlying algorithm. The revised optimization budget is an experimental-setting change.

E1.justification: v2 adds image-pair similarity scoring and ranking as an evaluated task through DiffED in Section 6.2 and Appendix E. v1 used images for interpolation and sampling-trajectory demonstrations. The represented domains remain the one-dimensional Gaussian mixture, ImageNet-512 images, and the two-dihedral-angle alanine-dipeptide landscape.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with LPIPS, SSIM and Euclidean image distance, plus fixed-length MCMC, variable-length MCMC and Doob's Lagrangian for molecular paths. The PF-ODE sampling comparison remains, while v1's SLERP interpolation comparisons disappear. Holdijk et al. and Raja et al. are discussed as excluded candidates in v2, so they are not evaluated baseline additions.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate 20 image pairs from each of 10 ImageNet classes and 1,000 molecular paths per method, reporting similarity correlations, mean MaxEnergy, a numerical lower bound and energy-evaluation counts. Separately, the stated image-interpolation budget changes from 350 steps with 16 curve points plus 250 steps with 64 points to 200 steps with 16 points. The retained illustrative eight-path molecular recipe should not be confused with the new benchmark.

E4.justification: v1's decoded-interpolation case study comparing SLERP sharpness against geodesic semantic preservation is removed. v2 adds the 'Space bar' image-pair ranking case study, qualitative molecular path-diversity comparisons, and Appendix G's account of baseline divergence and collapse across attempted configurations. The low-variance and region-avoidance demonstrations remain, without a new systematic ablation of the proposed method.

E5.justification: v2 Table 1 introduces means with ± values for molecular MaxEnergy, whereas v1 supplies qualitative paths without comparable uncertainty summaries. v2 states 1,000 paths per method but does not define the ± quantities or report seed-level training repetitions. Both versions retain the separate statement about generating eight independent illustrative paths.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports DiffED correlations of approximately -7% with LPIPS and 53% with SSIM. Table 1 adds MaxEnergy results of 37.66 ± 0.61 for spacetime geodesics, 42.54 ± 7.42 for fixed-length MCMC, 58.11 ± 18.51 for variable-length MCMC, and 66.24 ± 1.01 for Doob's Lagrangian, against a 36.42 lower bound. These are new comparisons, not same-setting gains over v1. The earlier SLERP sharpness/semantic-change findings are removed.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition B.1 and its proof that pullback geodesics under a bijective decoder decode to straight data-space segments. Section 5 adds the argument that terminal-noise memorylessness collapses the Fisher-Rao metric. The exponential-family and KL derivations are largely retained and reorganized. v1 Appendix F's KL Fisher-Rao flow lemma and proof are removed, along with its explicit pullback-versus-information-geometry complexity comparison.

C1.justification: v1 principally motivates information geometry through tractable computation and demonstrates interpolation and molecular applications. v2's abstract and introduction additionally claim fundamental limitations of pullback geometry, terminal-noise metric collapse, and Diffusion Edit Distance as a principal application. Molecular claims expand from demonstrating feasible paths to competitiveness with specialized methods, with an outperformance claim in Table 1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of geometric edit cost versus perceptual similarity, the dimensional explanation for pullback failure, and the coverage tradeoff of low-variance paths. It adds DiffED's computational-cost limitation and baseline-reproduction qualifications. Conversely, v1's blurry-interpolation discussion and optimization hypothesis disappear, as does its explicit warning that annealed Langevin paths only approximately follow the intended changing marginals. The near-clean-endpoint instability limitation remains.

D1.justification: The advertised code repository changes, and v2 updates the image-interpolation recipe and reported A100 runtime from approximately 50 to 6 minutes under the reduced budget. It adds a smaller-checkpoint runtime suggestion and baseline implementation/reproduction information in Appendix G, although exact successful baseline configurations remain unspecified. Most network architectures, training recipes, molecular settings and the JAX listing are retained.

R1.justification: Positioning shifts from avoiding expensive pullback computations to establishing their geometric limitations. v2 adds substantive connections to Domingo-Enrich et al. on memorylessness and Lobashev et al. on information geometry, alongside image-metric and MCMC references. It removes the discussion of score-based data-manifold analyses and its associated citations. The manifold-aware diffusion discussion is condensed and relocated to Section 3, rather than eliminated.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten. The earlier background/method sequence becomes separate diffusion background, Riemannian geometry, pullback-collapse and information-geometry sections. Exponential-family exposition and proofs are reorganized into the appendices, image interpolation is reframed around DiffED, and the societal-impact discussion moves into a main-text ethics statement. This is substantial narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: v2 adds the pullback-decoding schematic, molecular results table and four-method path figure. The earlier statistical-manifold schematic and SLERP comparison panels are removed. Image presentation changes from endpoint/peak-noise panels and decoded comparisons to full geodesic strips and metric-ranked image pairs. Sampling and constrained-path figures remain, with relocations and renumbering. These changes substantially revise the visual exposition.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the geometric motivation with the pullback theorem and adds quantitative checks beyond v1's illustrative validation, including the informative weak relationship between DiffED and LPIPS. The gains are limited by unresolved baseline-reproduction problems in Appendix G and undefined uncertainty quantities in Table 1. Removing v1's explicit caveat about approximate transition-path marginals also weakens qualification of the molecular application. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
